description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As the first machine learning engineer on a founding team at an agricultural technology company, you will build the models and data foundation that help growers make informed operational decisions. You will bring fragmented farm data together and evaluate models against real-world outcomes.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Audit and integrate historical data from farm systems, identifying available signals and data gaps.

 - Build forecasting, performance analysis, and operational efficiency tools for growers.

 - Develop rigorous backtesting and evaluation frameworks to assess model accuracy before deployment.

 - Create privacy-first, anonymized datasets that enable farms to benefit from shared insights.

 - Partner with an agent engineer to deliver actionable insights through the product.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Two to four years of engineering experience, including shipping production ML models that inform real decisions.

 - Strong Python and SQL skills, with fluency in pandas or polars, scikit-learn, gradient boosting, and forecasting libraries.

 - Experience with tabular or time-series data, data pipelines, and tools that explain model behavior.

 - Careful model evaluation skills, including understanding data leakage, backtesting, and production readiness.

 - Ability to explain model outputs and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders and investigate users' operational problems.

 - Daily experience building with AI and interest in combining LLMs and agents with classical ML.

 - Experience in agriculture, weather, supply chain, or other physical-world forecasting is helpful, as is experience with privacy-preserving data approaches.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $170,000 to $200,000 annually, plus 1% equity with four-year vesting and a one-year cliff. Healthcare benefits are provided. Visa sponsorship is not available; candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, five days a week. Travel to farms in Washington, Oregon, and California is expected for about one week per quarter.
